title: कनाडा निवासी NRI को फेक आईडी से फंसाया, 50 हजार डॉलर की मांग, गाजियाबाद पुलिस का सेक्सटॉर्शन गैंग पर बड़ा एक्शन

reading.body:
This is a sextortion and blackmail operation, not a failure of a model in a deployed product. The reported use of AI sits at the point of threat: police say the gang threatened to circulate AI-generated obscene videos alongside footage recorded during a video call. The AI output was never meant to be believed by a general audience, only by one targeted person, and its purpose was coercion rather than deception at scale.

The impersonation happened earlier and without AI. A fake Facebook profile was used to make first contact on Messenger, and the recording was made during a video call on September 10. The AI-generated material entered as leverage after the fact, when the demand for $50,000 was made. Catching this kind of operation depends on victim reporting and on financial tracing, not on content detection, because the harm is carried out through private messages and payment channels. The victim went to the cybercrime team on September 17, and the accused's mobile number was already linked to 40 cyber fraud complaints.

What is not established is the specific role each arrested person played, whether any AI tool has been identified or attributed, and whether the AI-generated videos were ever produced or sent. The charges are allegations, an FIR is not a finding, and the associates reported as absconding have not been located.

reports.title: Jamia Millia student among 4 held for using AI deepfakes to extort money from NRI
4 arrested for ₹6.5 crore extortion racket in Ghaziabad
कनाडा निवासी NRI को फेक आईडी से फंसाया, 50 हजार डॉलर की मांग, गाजियाबाद पुलिस का सेक्सटॉर्शन गैंग पर बड़ा एक्शन

summary:
A Jamia Millia Islamia student named Md Faisal and three associates from Muzaffarnagar were arrested in Ghaziabad for allegedly extorting a Canada-based NRI. Police said the gang created a fake Facebook profile, contacted the victim on Messenger, recorded him in a compromising position during a video call on September 10, then demanded $50,000, about Rs 4.7 crore, while threatening to circulate the footage and AI-generated obscene videos. The victim reported the matter to the cybercrime team on September 17, and the accused's mobile number was linked to 40 cyber fraud complaints.

Police registered an FIR under the BNS and IT Act, and four gang members were arrested on Friday while some associates remain absconding. Investigators said the gang had been active since 2023, used mule accounts and AI videos to target victims in India and abroad, and was linked to at least 130 bank accounts holding Rs 6.6 crore.
